evidence.finding: Around lines 276-278, _strict_empty_like expands x.shape into a tuple and dispatches torch.empty(tuple, device, dtype). The hot contiguous non-conj-bit output allocation goes through this general-shape helper.

Around lines 205-206, the contiguous non-conj-bit fast path is the only path that calls _strict_empty_like; the conj-bit and strided paths already call torch.empty(input.shape, ...) directly. Only this branch needs to change.

Current candidate feedback: full checks pass, candidate-only geometric speed is 0.99405 (no improvement), and all six timing cases remain 32-33us, so the prior device-lookup-removal hypothesis is not confirmed; host allocation overhead on the hot path remains an untested explanation. This is task feedback, not paired profiling.

Strict Triton storage policy allows allocation-only torch.empty_like, so the hot allocation can be expressed directly without a tuple-shape torch.empty dispatch and without bypassing the Triton copy kernel.
Full KGS is evaluation evidence from the old package use, not paired host profiling; it does not by itself establish the allocation mechanism.

hypothesis: On the dense contiguous non-conj-bit path, _strict_empty_like expands the shape into a tuple and calls torch.empty, adding host-side shape/dispatch allocation overhead. Replacing only that call with a direct independent contiguous torch.empty_like(input, memory_format=torch.contiguous_format) may lower per-call host cost and improve the 32-33us timing cases. This is inferred from the code diff, not from measured host profiling.
change: In run(), for the existing contig and not has_bit branch, replace out = _strict_empty_like(input) with out = torch.empty_like(input, memory_format=torch.contiguous_format). Keep the Triton copy kernel call and all other paths (conj-bit, strided, zero-numel) unchanged; still return a fresh independent contiguous tensor and never alias the input.
expected: If host allocation overhead is material, the six timing cases should drop below 32-33us and candidate-only geometric speed should exceed 1.0. If the device copy dominates, timings and geometric speed should stay flat. Fresh-allocation and non-aliasing semantics must remain identical.
validation: Run preflight on the edited candidate, then evaluate with the standard full checks/timing suite. Compare the six timing cases and candidate-only geometric speed against the current 32-33us / 0.99405 baseline, and confirm copy correctness (independent contiguous output, no input aliasing) across contiguity and conj-bit cases.
